themes_detail.label: Police Calls Spike This Week
themes_detail.summary: Non-Emergency Police Matter complaints surged to 6 THIS WEEK, triple the 2.0 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 4.0), signaling a sudden uptick in incidents requiring police intervention across Morningside Heights/Hamilton Heights.
evidence: 6 Non-Emergency Police Matter complaints THIS WEEK vs. 2.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (200% spike, z-score 4.0)
No recent Reddit discussions or news mentions of broader safety issues to cross-reference
Spike appears isolated to this current week with no prior escalation pattern visible in 8-week baseline
reporting_angles: Call 311 records to determine what types of incidents drove this week's spike—are residents reporting street harassment, domestic disputes, or something else?
Contact NYPD 26th Precinct community affairs to ask if there's a reported crime pattern or incident cluster matching complaint dates

themes_detail.label: Commercial Noise Eruption
themes_detail.summary: Commercial Noise complaints jumped 184% two weeks ago (73 complaints vs. 25.8 weekly average, z-score: 4.02), suggesting either new or intensified business activity—restaurant construction, music venues, or street-level commercial operations—disrupting residents.
evidence: 73 Commercial Noise complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 25.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (184% spike, z-score 4.02)
Commercial Noise ranks #9 on 90-day volume list (414 total complaints), indicating it's a persistent category spiking upward
No corresponding Reddit discussions or recent news coverage of commercial noise issues in the district
reporting_angles: Cross-reference DOB permits filed in the last 30 days (366 total filings, mostly alterations) to identify new construction or renovations triggering noise complaints
Interview residents near commercial corridors (Amsterdam Ave, 125th St) to identify the specific business or venue type causing disruption

themes_detail.label: Food Safety Violations Jump
themes_detail.summary: Food Establishment complaints spiked 300% last week (6 complaints vs. 1.5 weekly average, z-score: 4.5), indicating potential health code violations or unsanitary conditions at restaurants or food vendors in the neighborhood.
evidence: 6 Food Establishment complaints last week vs. 1.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (300% spike, z-score 4.5)
Unsanitary Condition is #5 on 90-day volume list (713 complaints), suggesting broader sanitation issues in the district
Community Board has filed repeated budget requests for 'Other programs to address public health issues' with DOHMH—unresolved need
reporting_angles: Obtain NYC Health Department inspection records for the past 2 weeks to identify which establishments triggered complaints and what violations were found
Interview health inspectors or DOHMH about whether there's a pattern (e.g., temporary vendor surge, restaurant under-staffing post-COVID, pest infestations)

themes_detail.label: Encampment Surge (3 weeks ago)
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints surged 789% three weeks ago (10 complaints vs. 1.1 weekly average, z-score: 5.78), marking a significant but slightly-dated spike in homeless encampments or tent cities; trend status THIS WEEK unclear and warrants follow-up.
evidence: 10 Encampment complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 1.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (789% spike, z-score 5.78)
Blocked Driveway also spiked 197% simultaneously (13 complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 4.4 avg), suggesting street/sidewalk obstruction tied to encampments
Community Board budget request for 'Allocate funds for outreach services to homebound older adults' (unsolved, repeated request) suggests underlying social services gap
reporting_angles: Check whether encampment spike from 3 weeks ago has persisted or subsided—obtain most recent week's 311 complaint data to assess trend continuation
Interview BRC (Bowery Residents' Committee) or other homeless outreach providers working in Morningside/Hamilton Heights about encampment demographics and service gaps

themes_detail.label: Building Code Violations Cluster
themes_detail.summary: Three high-z-score 311 spikes converged 2 weeks ago (Outside Building +860%, Unsanitary Animal +700%, SPIT inspection requests +700%, z-scores 7.72–4.95), suggesting deteriorating building conditions, pest infestations, or code violations warranting inspection authority attention.
evidence: Outside Building complaints: 6 (2 weeks ago) vs. 0.6 weekly average (860% spike, z-score 7.72—highest severity)
Unsanitary Animal Private Property: 5 (2 weeks ago) vs. 0.6 avg (700% spike, z-score 6.29)
SPIT (Special Projects Inspection Team) requests: 4 (2 weeks ago) vs. 0.5 avg (700% spike, z-score 4.95)—residents actively requesting deeper city inspections
Community Board budget request for 'Animal and pest control requests including reducing rat and mosquito populations' (unsolved, repeated request) confirms systemic problem
reporting_angles: Request DOB and HPD inspection records for buildings flagged with SPIT requests 2 weeks ago—identify which properties have violations and what remediation is required
Interview residents in affected buildings to document living conditions; contact HPD/DOB about enforcement timeline for violations found
